subject: SIG Questionnaire Initiation — Acme Corp (Post-demo follow-up)
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Turner <michael.turner@acme-corp.com>, Linda Cho <linda.cho@acme-corp.com>
Date: 2026-01-15T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: SIG Questionnaire Initiation — Acme Corp (Post-demo follow-up)

Hi Michael / Linda,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really appreciate the time. Per our conversation, I’m starting the vendor security questionnaire process so your team can validate Redwood for the Acme integration. Attached is a short SIG starter packet (Redwood_SIG_Starter.pdf) and a link to our security overview: https://drive.google.com/redwood/security/sig-starter.

Quick answers up front to the common asks we discussed:
- SOC 2: Redwood completed SOC 2 Type I in 2024 and we are currently undergoing SOC 2 Type II (expected completion: 2026-03). Our SOC 2 status and timeline are documented in the starter packet.
- GDPR/HIPAA: We have GDPR controls and DPAs available; we can support HIPAA-covered workloads under a BAA and via Private/Dedicated deployment options.
- Data residency: Hosted deployments are region-aware; Dedicated/Private options can be provisioned in customer-chosen regions.

To move things forward, could you confirm which intake you prefer us to fill: SIG/CAIQ/custom form? I’ve attached a suggested starter response template (Redwood_SIG_Response_Draft.docx) to speed things up.

A few clarifying questions from our side to help prioritize:
1) Are there specific control families you want completed first (e.g., encryption key management, subprocessor list, network segmentation)?
2) Do you require customer-managed keys (CMK) for encryption at rest for the initial rollout, or would provider-managed keys be acceptable during pilot?
3) Any required timeline for the completed questionnaire (e.g., internal review deadline)?

If it helps, I can loop in our security and legal leads (cc’ed) to answer any detailed questions. Proposing a short 30-min call this week to walk through the SIG — when is your team available?

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Attachment: Redwood_SIG_Starter.pdf (PDF)
From: Michael Turner <michael.turner@acme-corp.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
Cc: Linda Cho <linda.cho@acme-corp.com>, security@acme-corp.com
Date: 2026-01-16T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Re: SIG Questionnaire Initiation — Acme Corp (Post-demo follow-up)

Hi Camila — thanks for the recap and the starter packet. Attaching our standard intake (Acme_SIG_Filled.xlsx) with a few pre-filled fields from our side. A couple of clarifications/questions:

- Your SOC 2 timeline is helpful; for our procurement review we’ll flag the ongoing Type II audit but would like to understand compensating controls you have in place today. Can you point me to any interim evidence (e.g., internal control matrix, recent penetration test report)?

- Subprocessors: We need a current list of subprocessors (or a link to a maintained list). If you have a published subprocessor page, please share.

- Encryption / Key management: Our security team prefers SSE with customer-managed keys (CMK) where possible. Does Redwood support CMK in hosted or only in Dedicated/Private deployments?

- Data residency: Acme requires EU data residency for EU customer data. Can you confirm which deployment types can guarantee EU-only storage for data at rest and backups?

We’re happy to do a 30-min session to walk through the SIG; available Jan 20 10:00–12:00 ET or Jan 21 afternoon ET.

Thanks,
Michael Turner
Senior Security Analyst, Acme Corp
michael.turner@acme-corp.com
Attachment: Acme_SIG_Filled.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Camila Reyes <camila.reyes@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Turner <michael.turner@acme-corp.com>, Linda Cho <linda.cho@acme-corp.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-01-16T11:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: SIG Questionnaire Initiation — Acme Corp (Post-demo follow-up)

Thanks Michael — great questions. Looping in Rishi (Security) and Stephanie (Legal) to provide short, authoritative answers and any interim evidence. Quick answers from my side while they jump in:

- Interim evidence: We can provide our most recent penetration test summary and an internal control matrix for the SOC 2 controls in scope. Rishi — can you attach the PT summary and control matrix?

- Subprocessors: We maintain a published, regularly-updated subprocessor list. Link: https://drive.google.com/redwood/security/subprocessors and I’ve also attached a CSV snapshot (redwood_subprocessors.csv) for your intake.

- CMK / KMS: For hosted (multi-tenant) API, default is provider-managed keys; Customer-Managed Keys (CMK) are available for Dedicated and Private deployment modes via KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS) and require contractual terms (we can scope in the KMS support in the Dedicated/Private offering). Stephanie — happy to confirm language we need in the contract/BAA.

- EU data residency: Dedicated and Private deployments can be provisioned in EU regions and configured to store data at rest and backups in-region. For hosted customers, we route EU customer data to EU regions by default but we would need to confirm backup geography for specific retention policies.

Next steps I propose:
1) Rishi/Stephanie share the PT summary, control matrix, and any redlined contract language we’ll need for CMK/BAA.
2) We (Redwood + Acme) run a 30-min SIG walkthrough on Jan 20 10:30 ET (proposed) — confirm if that works.
3) We’ll return a filled SIG (using your Acme_SIG_Filled.xlsx) within ~5 business days after the walkthrough.

Camila Reyes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Attachments: redwood_subprocessors.csv (CSV), Redwood_SIG_Response_Draft.docx (DOCX)
